Sancyranus seized this opportunity to declaim against the regulars and issued that famous pamphlet on the *Hierarchy* under the pseudonym of *Petrus Aurelius*. The work was well-received as long as the author remained hidden, and it was approved by the Synod of the Gallican Clergy on April 27, 1641, and committed to the press at their expense. Antoine Godeau, Bishop of Grasse, added a eulogy in which the author is proclaimed an "invincible defender of bishops, a most fierce lover of the truth, a most just vindicator of the Hierarchy, and a theologian raised in the bosom of ancestral theology." Sancyranus's modesty did not have enough strength to allow him to remain hidden any longer amidst such commendation of himself and his work. But when the author was discovered, a blush covered their faces, and all that pomp of words eventually vanished even from the book *Gallia Christiana*.

Indeed, he proved himself a candidate of ancestral theology in the book condemned on April 23, 1654: *Familiar Theology, or a brief explanation of the mysteries of the Faith*
